dispatch.headline: Living Whale Liver Demands Pork Fat
dispatch.body:
ZURICH-ON-STILTS - City elders ordered BioBaleen to haul a forty-tonne fake whale liver through elevated streets using wooden rollers and pig fat.

Chief Ruler Sun-Hee Bergstrom ruled that municipal crews must butter six miles of stone paths with rendered fat every four hours. Flying the organ by heavy drone took fifteen minutes. However, the panel decided hovering meat ruined city sky views.

The tissue was grown to strain plastic from mountain runoff. Moving it manually across upper terraces will take eleven days and dismantle three cafes.

"Traders along the main street may find the warm fat smell foul," wrote Bergstrom. "Yet an organ this body size gets no exemption just because it lacks feet."

It has no feet.

Events shifted when engineers noticed the tissue moving on its own. Friction from timber rollers and warm grease revived old muscle reflexes within the meat. By flexing its left side, the organ now navigates bends to chase pure fat.

"We thought oiling the road was a chore," said crew chief Kenji Sato, watching the wet mass slide past a tea shop. "Now we know if we fall behind, the liver gets angry."

It wants more fat.

"Yesterday it chased a butter cart up the hill," Sato added. "We had to throw it three blocks of tallow to save the driver."

City rulers have now granted the meat full right of way over all public traffic.
dispatch.scene: Municipal workers in rubber aprons pour bucketfuls of liquid lard onto cobblestones as a glistening forty-tonne whale liver rolls past a medieval clock tower on wooden logs.
dispatch.premise: The High Court has ordered a biotech firm to physically haul a 40-ton lab-grown whale liver through Zurich’s medieval alleyways on rollers, requiring municipal crews to grease six miles of cobblestone with lard every four hours.

revisions.reason: The original draft suffered from legal jargon, present-day props, forbidden terminology, and excessive sentence length. It also relied on cliché phrasing and lacked punchy short sentences.
revisions.headline: High Court Orders Street Greasing For Mobile Whale Liver
revisions.body:
ZURICH-ON-STILTS - The High Court of Cantonal Equity has ordered BioBaleen AG to physically haul a forty-tonne lab-grown whale liver through the medieval alleyways of the elevated city using wooden rollers and municipal lard.

Under the ruling handed down by Chief Magistrate Sun-Hee Bergstrom, municipal crews must grease six miles of preserved cobblestone with rendered pig fat every four hours to ensure smooth transit. The synthetic organ, cultured to filter microplastics from alpine floodwaters, was denied aerial transport permits after the tribunal held that hovering heavy offal violated municipal skyway aesthetics.

Counsel for BioBaleen had argued that transporting the massive tissue via heavy-lift quadcopter would take fifteen minutes, whereas manual rolling across the city's upper terraces will require eleven days of continuous greasing and the temporary dismantling of three outdoor cafes.

"The court acknowledges that shopkeepers along the Spiegelgasse may find the combined aroma of warm lard and cultured hepatic tissue disagreeable during trading hours," wrote Chief Magistrate Bergstrom in the majority opinion. "However, an organ of this magnitude cannot be exempted from medieval livestock right-of-way obligations simply because it lacks feet."

The proceedings took an unexpected turn when municipal engineers revealed that the liver is no longer merely being moved; it has begun steering itself. The continuous friction of the timber dowels, combined with the warmth of the grease, has reawakened primitive metabolic reflexes within the tissue. By selectively contracting its left lobe, the organ is actively navigating hairpins and pursuing the freshest lard deposits.

"We initially viewed the four-hour re-greasing schedule as a tedious civil burden," stated senior municipal crew chief Kenji Sato, watching the glistening grey mass squeeze past an apothecary. "We now recognise that if the lard team falls behind schedule, the liver grows agitated and begins rolling uphill towards the dairy market."
